description: COMPLETE the mixed512 (shape 6) peel by handling the un-probed REPEATED subset with a MULTI-LEVEL projector (generalizing the proven two-level path). brief-33 flagged it: after dense(264,k352)+clustered(37,two-level)+psd(76,k256) peels, the mixed512 rest (~263 mats on cuSOLVER) includes ~45 REPEATED matrices (PR~286, generated with <=16 distinct eigenvalues = 16 eigenvalue LEVELS by reference.py's 'repeated' case: base=linspace(-1,1,groups<=16) repeated). This is EXACTLY the structure the two-level (+-1) projector exploits, generalized to G levels: A has G distinct eigenvalues lambda_g, so the spectral projector onto level g is a low-degree polynomial, and the eigenspaces are the ranges of (prod_{h!=g}(A-lambda_h I)) applied to a random probe. STEP 1 (probe): on the mixed512 repeated subset (classify by PR~286 window, distinct from psd[37,48)/dense[51.6,58.1]/clustered), (a) detect the G levels cheaply (histogram of diag(Q^T A Q) after a rough projection, or the distinct values of a few Rayleigh quotients), (b) measure whether a G-level projector (G small, <=16) + per-level CQR + block L-assignment beats cuSOLVER's marginal ~0.24ms/mat at n=512 b640, like the 2-level path does on clustered512. STEP 2 (if positive): add a repeated-peel band to _eigh_mixed_peel routing PR~286 matrices to a _eigh_multilevel(A, levels) that reuses the two-level machinery per level; rest still cuSOLVER; per-matrix residual-gated fallback. If the multi-level projector is too expensive at G=16 (16 poly applications) or the levels aren't cheaply detectable (probe negative), refute cleanly. DISTINCT from brief-33 (psd), brief-28 (dense/clustered), brief-20 (two-level=G=2 special case). PURE-TORCH (classifier + projector, reuse _eigh_twolevel structure); no nvcc; GPU-light. Forks best 5c66a54b3; do NOT regress the existing dense/clustered/psd peels or any homogeneous shape; no 'stream' substring; verify 39/39 + quiet re-bench beats 35401 (or refute).

MULTI-LEVEL PROJECTOR for mixed512 repeated subset -- REFUTED cleanly with measured cost estimate (1 committed trial a8254fcbb + 6 probes). Band DISABLED (_MIXED_PEEL_REPEATED=False), machinery committed as the measured artifact behind the residual gate. Verdict: 39/39 PASS; geomean 35566/35569us (parent 35603, within noise); shape6 132490us == parent 132439 (band inert, ZERO regression on any of 13 shapes). grep stream=0, pure-torch, no nvcc.

WHY REFUTED -- DECISIVE ECONOMICS (the hard wall): the repeated subset is EXACTLY 50 mats (PR=285.94 constant, cleanly isolated: band<=253.67 below, clustered=512 above -- window [265,400) has ~30/~110 safety gaps). Peeling all 50 drops the cuSOLVER 'rest' call only 75.17->67.49ms = 7.68ms MARGINAL (robust, median of 5, tight). Ceiling on the geomean win from a FREE, PERFECT projector = 7.68ms = 0.058% of shape6 = 0.0217% of the 35.4ms geomean -- BELOW the 1% noise floor. No projector engineering can make this measurable; the subset is simply too small (50 of 640 mats, and n=512 cuSOLVER marginal is only ~0.15ms/mat here).

WHY REFUTED -- COST + CORRECTNESS (secondary confirmations): n=512 => G=16 exact levels linspace(-1,1,16), 32 eigenvalues each (verified). The Lagrange projector prod_{h!=g}(A-lambda_h I) needs DOUBLE application (like _eigh_twolevel's P+^2) -- 1x leaks (mid-level leakage 9e-3), 2x is clean (6.8e-5). (1) COST: double-proj = G*(G-1)*2 = 480 FP64 bmms + CQR + NS = ~28-31ms = ~4x the 7.68ms ceiling. Matches brief's own gate ('projector >~11ms can't win'): 28 >> 7.7. (2) ORTHOGONALITY fails 50/50 at G=16 (orth 1.1-2.7 >> 4.6e-3 gate) with BOTH block-diagonal AND joint CQR+NS -- the 16 near-degenerate levels (spacing 0.133) leave ~6.8e-5 cross-level leakage that sums over the L1 orth-norm across 16x16 block pairs x 512 cols; AND the projector column-norm dynamic range (endpoint ~0.5 vs middle ~1e-4, since middle Lagrange denoms ~1e-5) makes the joint Gram ill-conditioned/singular (grouped-levels variant hit a Cholesky non-PD failure at order 229). The EIGENVALUE side is exact (eig 1.8e-6) -- levels resolve perfectly -- but eigenVECTORS in the degenerate 32-dim blocks can't be made mutually orthonormal to gate in FP64. No smaller-G subset exists (all 50 are G=16).

VARIANTS TRIED (all refuted): times=1 (eig fails), times=2/3 (orth fails), block-diag CQR+NS, joint CQR+NS, joint-CQR + jointNS x2/3, Lagrange-normalized (orth 0.76 still fails), FP32 projector (worse), grouped-levels Gg=2/4/8 (Cholesky non-PD -- ill-conditioned span). FP32 projector ~14ms still >> 7.68ms ceiling anyway.

OPEN DIRECTIONS for the manager (NOT pursued -- off this brief; all bounded by the same 0.0217% geomean ceiling so LIKELY not worth a follow-up on THIS subset): (1) A fused megakernel G-level projector could cut the ~28ms projector cost, but even 0ms saves only 7.68ms = 0.02% geomean -- unmeasurable. (2) The orthogonality failure could in principle be fixed by a reduced eigh of the full Qy-span (Bk = Qy^T A Qy then eigh, lift) instead of block/joint CQR -- but that reintroduces a cuSOLVER call on the subset, defeating the purpose, and still can't beat the 7.68ms ceiling. (3) The REAL lever on shape6 remains elsewhere: the mixed512 'rest' still runs ~213 mats on cuSOLVER (rankdef 32 + nearrank 45 at PR~83, spectrum 40 at PR~111, band 50 at PR~247, rowscale 46 at PR~27). brief-33 noted rankdef/nearrank [62,100)->k384 was refuted at the current split-mega orth ceiling (~k=300); if a brief RAISES that inner-solve orth ceiling (>=k384), the ~77 rankdef/nearrank mats have a much larger cuSOLVER marginal (~0.24ms/mat x77 ~18ms, ~2.4x the repeated subset) and could genuinely peel. band(50)/rowscale(46) are likely too flat (PR247/PR27) but un-probed at their own k. (4) Shape6 is only the 2nd-biggest mixed term; the homogeneous shapes 3/8 (n=512 dense/rankdef) and 4/12 (n=1024) already win via low-rank -- larger absolute levers than any mixed512 sub-class peel.
